html:
Roman Stoic philosopher, playwright and statesman, who was tutor and adviser to the emperor Nero.

He was born in Corduba (Córdoba) in Spain to a rich family and trained in Rome as a speaker. In 41 CE Claudius exiled him to Corsica. In 49 CE Agrippina called him back to teach her son Nero. When Nero became emperor in 54 CE, Seneca and the guard commander Burrus guided him, and his first years were seen as good. Seneca grew immensely rich, which critics thought odd for a Stoic.

As Nero turned to murder, Seneca tried to withdraw, in 62 CE. In 65 CE Nero accused him of a part in the Pisonian conspiracy and ordered him to kill himself. He cut his veins, and Tacitus describes his slow, calm death.

His writings include essays on anger, calm and the shortness of life, the Letters to Lucilius, an account of the earthquake at Pompeii in his Natural Questions, and blood-soaked tragedies that shaped Elizabethan drama.
sum: Roman Stoic philosopher, playwright and statesman, who was tutor and adviser to the emperor Nero.
